scope: Exactly one independent mobile pixel-review batch using seven existing screenshots and the existing en-mobile DOM view; no source, SCI, ZHEN or figure-semantic re-review.

structure.countBasis: User-supplied facts, with object/paragraph/figure/exercise counts corroborated by the reused mobile DOM view. Five separators are visible in the downscaled whole-page capture; the DOM boxes list does not enumerate HR elements.

observations.detail: The title wraps into three lines, ending with a short 'light' line. All words fit within the side margins, with no clipped glyphs or collision with the printed-page line. Body text is clearly readable at this capture's full displayed size; line breaks and paragraph gaps remain distinct.

At overview scale, the five separator rules have visible space around adjoining prose. Paragraphs, bold runs, figures and their numbered captions remain in coherent reading order. No visible prose/figure collision, page-edge spill or caption overlap was found. The mobile DOM reports page width 390 and heading/prose boxes contained within x=16 through x=374.

The heading, Light in/Light out labels and lower rotation label are clearly readable and separated from the plate and arrows. Plate, beam, arrowheads and right-side eye are fully framed with white-space margins. DOM label scale is 17.9 px at actual media width 358.

All three vertically stacked panels are fully framed. Panel headings, plate numbers, repeated Axes face view labels, direction marks and Light out/Dimmer/No light out labels are distinguishable. No label collides with an adjacent panel or leaves the image; beam/plate intersections are part of the drawing, not incoherent layout overlap. DOM label scale is 17.9 px at actual media width 358.

The full plate, outer horizontal arrowheads and central directional arrows fit inside the capture. The lower Possible transverse directions label is readable and separated from the drawing. Central arrow convergence does not cover text. DOM label scale is 17.9 px at actual media width 358.

The beam outline, plate, vertical arrow and horizontal arrowheads are fully framed. The p label is readable and does not collide with the outline or beam arrow; the lower One transverse direction label has clear space. DOM label scale is 17.9 px at actual media width 358.

The visible left portion has readable Changing directions, First box, Moving end and Vertical opening labels, with clear separation from the rope and first box. Several longer labels and the rope continue through the right viewport edge. This is the supplied fixed-640 scroll presentation inside a 358-wide mobile figure area, not evidence that the SVG canvas itself truncates those labels. No incoherent overlap was found in the visible portion.

The reused mobile DOM records 640x444 actual media and 16 px labels. Second box, turned 90 degrees, Sideways opening and Fixed end have recorded bounds within media x=16 through x=656; Fixed end spans page x=562.8671875 through x=633.1328125. The longer lower labels also have bounds inside the media. These are existing structural endpoint-label evidence, not newly inspected right-end pixels or proof of a tested scroll gesture.

Despite the filename and definitionScreenshot field, this image shows the lesson top, title and introductory prose, not the later polarization definition. It was used only for full-size top-of-page readability.

limitations: The view_image tool automatically downscaled en-mobile-whole.png from 390x12243 to 191x6000. That view supports overall spacing, order and gross clipping review, not a native-resolution readability certification for all 43 paragraphs.

The polarization-viewport capture is a top-of-lesson viewport, not a definition viewport. Later definition typography was visible only in the downscaled overview; no new screenshot, crop or reopen was performed.

Figure 212 was pixel-reviewed only at its captured left scroll position. Offscreen endpoint labels rely on the hash-bound existing mobile DOM evidence; no right-end pixels or scrolling interaction were independently tested.
Source-bound Chinese ARIA labels for Figures 208-212 are retained and disclosed in the reused report. This PASS is not full English accessibility approval.
Existing DOM evidence records platform Arial rendering and effective SVG label sizes. No embedded-font or embedded-raster-glyph certification is claimed.
This review reuses isolated-headless/offline evidence only and does not certify headed, live-production, device-specific or additional-viewport behavior.
Approved SCI, ZHEN, source fidelity and figure semantics were not reopened or re-evaluated. The PASS applies only to this bounded mobile pixel scope.

conclusion: PASS for the bounded mobile pixel scope: no blocking visible readability, wrapping, spacing, framing, label-overlap or unintended-clipping defect found. Capture-position, downscaling, scroll-endpoint, accessibility and font limitations remain explicit.
